messages:
lee: Quick help needed for Nimbus POC. Their Vector sink exports to our drain but trace_id/traceparent fields are blank and they see intermittent 429s. Can eng triage?
maya: On it. Are they using batch mode? Any sample event?
lee: Yes batch enabled. Sample LA event: {"time":"2026-03-18T15:02:10Z","service":"nimbus-app","trace":"","req_id":"r_114x"}.
sam: Two likely causes: Vector batches multiple events per HTTP request (headers apply to request, not per-event), or our runtime is dropping headers during internal batching.
maya: Tests to run: 1) ask customer to curl a single event with `traceparent` header to /v1/logs/drain and confirm it appears. 2) we can temporarily bump their drain burst to smooth 429s.
emily: Opened quota ticket POCQ-221. I told customer about the curl test.
ops-bot: quota adjust applied for account nimbus-poc; change=q_221; drain burst=+2x for 4h.
lee: Customer ran curl with header; single-event shows trace present. So path works for single requests.
maya: That confirms batching path. Short fixes: a) set runtime flag `redwood.runtime.batch.keep_headers=true` for their instance, or b) change Vector to inject header into each event body before batching. Which is easier for them?
emily: Customer prefers us to toggle runtime while they modify config.
maya: OK I'll push the runtime toggle and restart. Deploy will post.
ops-bot: config apply started for nimbus-poc; id=ch_221a; rolling restart.
ops-bot: rolling restart complete; instance healthy.
emily: Customer re-ran tests — most events now have trace populated and 429s reduced. A few older queued events still empty.
lee: Great. Follow-ups: keep quota bump for 4h, ask customer to update Vector template to include `request.headers.traceparent`, and revert sampling/quota after. I'll update the POC doc.
maya: I'll monitor for the window. Close here unless we see more 429s.
